**Starts** once #66 is merged.

## Why

This is the first trip a simulated user (#66) plans on the live site. It does two things. It checks that the simulated user works well enough to record sessions for the corpus. And it leaves a whole planned trip in the server's Phoenix project, `road-trip-agent`, for agent evaluations (#53) to score.

The final itinerary isn't checked against domain model section 5.1. Places come from live Google results and from the workers' picks, so two good runs can pick two different motels. What's checked is how the simulated user behaved, and what the coordinator saved to the trip brief.

## Design

- [Simulated users README](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/simulated-users/README.md): how to set up, start, and check a run. Its sections "Set up a run", "Start a harness", and "Check a run" cover this issue.
- [The simulated user](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/issues/66): the San Francisco trip file, `simulated-users/trips/san-francisco.md`.
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 5.1: the San Francisco trip.

## Open questions

- ~~How much of the Claude Max plan (systems design, section 5) does a planning session use? Check the plan's usage bars in Claude's settings before and after the run. For a rough size, #66's local runs of this trip took 30 to 36 of the simulated user's messages, and 10 to 17 minutes.~~ Settled on 2026-11-04 in chat: not measured. Joe found that the local test sessions each used very little of the plan, and this run plays on Sonnet, which uses less.

## Do

- Run the San Francisco trip file with Claude Code and Sonnet, as the bot user `claude-code-sonnet`, with the `easygoing` persona, on the live site (`https://roadtrip.jjk3.com`). Set it up and start it headless, as the README says. First remove `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/claude-code-sonnet-san-francisco-easygoing/`, left from #66's local runs, since `npm run sim-setup` stops while it's there.
- Check the session as the README's "Check a run" says. There are three checks: the simulated user stuck to the trip file, it acted like a user, and the trip brief matches the trip file's facts. The README also says where to read the final trip brief, and which differences between runs are fine.
- If the session fails a check because of the setup, fix the setup, the trip file, the persona file, or the instructions, and run again. Mark the failed run in Phoenix, as the README says.
- File each app bug the run finds as a new issue. Don't fix it here.

## Done when

- A simulated session of the San Francisco trip is in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project.
- The simulated session passes the three checks above, and the results are in the PR.
- The app bugs found are filed as issues.

## Ends in

A PR, with any changes to the setup, the trip file, the persona file, or the instructions.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

## Why

This is the first time a whole trip is planned from start to finish, by the simulated user and then by Joe. It shows whether the app as a whole does what the design docs say.

## Design

- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 5.1: the San Francisco trip.

## Open questions

- How much of the Claude Max plan (systems design, section 5) does a planning session use? Check the plan's usage bars in Claude's settings before and after the run.

## Do

- Write the San Francisco trip script, with its changes along the way.
- Run it with the simulated user (#66), fix each problem in its report, and run it again. A fix that changes the design goes to Joe first.
- Joe then plans the same trip by hand on the deployed site (systems design, section 7).

## Done when

- The simulated run ends with the itinerary in domain model section 5.1: the same stays, nights, stops, places, and approvals. Each change along the way is handled as the design docs say.
- Joe's run ends the same way.
- Any problems still open are listed in the PR.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
